Well, how could I consider that? How could I possibly think it's not happening when I see it with my own two eyes, every single Sunday, every single family gathering? You’re asking me to doubt my own reality, doctor, and I just can't do that. I mean, think about it from my perspective. I've spent thirty-five years—thirty-five years!—building a life, raising children, keeping a home that you could eat off the floors of, and serving that church. I was the one who suggested we switch to the silk lilies for the winter services because the real ones were wilting too fast near the radiators! 

And now, you want me to think that maybe I'm just imagining that they're using the altar against me? That the parish committee isn't involved? It’s not just in my head! I told you, I came in here because I finally realized, I *knew* it, that my in-laws aren't just having a little disagreement with me. They are actively, deliberately using the altar and the entire parish committee to push me out. They want to completely erase me and make every single person in that congregation and in this family forget what I have done for them.

Well, no, not exactly. I mean... how could I? Who on earth would I even go to? If I go to the church leadership, who am I going to talk to? Father Thomas? Please! But... if I actually say it out loud to them, they’ll just do exactly what you just tried to do, doctor. They’ll tell me I’m making things up. They’ll use it as more ammunition.

That is exactly what they want! They want me to look unstable so they have an excuse to erase me completely and justify everything they've been doing behind my back. 

So, no. I haven't given them the satisfaction. I haven't said a single word to them about it because I know better than to walk right into their trap. I just sit back, and I watch them. I see it all happening, and I keep track of it. Every little slight, every ignored greeting, every time they change the schedule without telling me... I see it, but I haven't confronted them because that's exactly the opening they're waiting for.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, if you're asking if my husband thinks I'm seeing things or making things up, then yes, I suppose there is something else. But again, it’s just him being completely blind to what is right in front of his face! 

You see, I've been trying to get the house in order, especially with all this stress from the church, and I like things done a very specific way. My mother, God rest her soul, she taught me everything I know about keeping a proper home. She was an absolute stickler for details, just like me. And lately... well, on several nights recently, I've actually heard her. Clear as a bell! I was up late, probably around two or three in the morning, working on some floral arrangements for the dining room—because if I don't keep the house looking beautiful, it all just falls apart—and I heard her voice telling me exactly where to put the marigolds. Marigolds can be very tricky, you know, they have that very distinct scent and a bold color, so you have to balance them just right. And she was right there, her voice telling me exactly where the candles needed to go around them to catch the light properly. 

And then... well, there was this one time, just a few days ago, where I actually saw her. I was in the kitchen. I had just finished wiping down the counters—I always use a water and vinegar solution, by the way, it cuts through the grime so much better than those awful chemical sprays they sell at the supermarket now—and I looked up, and she was standing right there near the kitchen doorway. Just standing there! Wearing her old blue housecoat. 

I gasped, I really did, and my husband came shuffling out of the bedroom in his slippers, rubbing his eyes and grumbling about the noise. I pointed right at the doorway, right at her! And do you know what he said? He looked right at the spot, looked back at me, and told me no one was there. He told me I was just dreaming while I was awake and that it didn't make any sense. 

But I wasn't dreaming! How could I be dreaming when I was holding a damp sponge in my hand? I know my own mother's voice, and I know what I saw in my own kitchen doorway. He just doesn't pay attention to anything. He didn't see her, so suddenly it 'isn't true.' Just like he doesn't see what the parish committee is doing behind my back. It's always, 'Oh, you're just tired, go back to bed.' But I know she was there helping me with the marigolds and the candles. I know what I experienced, doctor, even if he wants to tell me it isn't real.

I was the one who suggested we switch to the silk lilies for the winter services because the real ones were wilting too fast near the radiators! \n\nAnd now, you want me to think that maybe I'm just imagining that they're using the altar against me? That the parish committee isn't involved? It’s not just in my head! I told you, I came in here because I finally realized, I *knew* it, that my in-laws aren't just having a little disagreement with me. They are actively, deliberately using the altar and the entire parish committee to push me out. They want to completely erase me and make every single person in that congregation and in this family forget what I have done for them. \n\nIf it wasn't happening the way I believe it is, then why did Susan—my sister-in-law, who I taught how to make a proper pie crust, by the way—why did she look right past me when they were handing out the bulletins last week? Why did the head of the committee suddenly decide that they didn't need my help organizing the spring bazaar? I've run that bazaar for over a decade! We raised enough money for a new roof in 2012 because of my silent auction idea! You don't just 'forget' to ask someone who did all that, unless it's on purpose. Unless you're trying to push them out. \n\nSo no, I don't think I'm wrong. I don't think it's just me misunderstanding things. People don't want to see it because it's ugly, doctor. It's an ugly truth that people who smile at you and take communion with you could be plotting to erase your entire legacy. My husband doesn't want to see it because it means confronting his own family, and he hates conflict. He’d rather just watch his golf and pretend everything is fine. But I can't pretend. I know what they're doing with the committee, I know what they're doing at the altar, and I know they want me gone and forgotten.\n\nDoctor: Have you taken any steps to address what you believe is happening, like confronting your in-laws or speaking to someone in the church about it?\n\nPatient: Well, no, not exactly. A beautiful rump roast with carrots and potatoes, cooked low and slow all afternoon, and my gravy—well, people used to ask for the recipe, but I never gave it out. But now? Now he’s over there eating her dry, overcooked chicken and probably listening to her poison him against me. They want me to look unstable so they have an excuse to erase me completely and justify everything they've been doing behind my back. \n\nSo, no. I haven't given them the satisfaction. ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, before all this nonsense with my in-laws and the church? No, I really can't say that I have. I've always been a very practical, grounded woman. You don't manage a household, raise children, and run a parish committee for decades by having your head in the clouds! I’ve always lived in the real world. 

But, you know, if you're trying to imply that I just walk around imagining things all the time, I have to stop you right there. Because I pay attention to myself, doctor, and I notice how things happen. Take my mother, for instance. Hearing her voice and seeing her in the doorway... that didn't just happen out of the blue, and it certainly isn't happening every day of my life. It really only happened during that one particular stretch of time recently. 

You see, during those weeks, I was barely sleeping at all. Maybe an hour or two a night, if that! I didn't even feel tired, though. I was just rushing around, day and night, getting the house absolutely perfect, scrubbing the baseboards, fixing the floral arrangements, because I felt—no, I was absolutely sure—that I had this incredibly special, sacred duty to fix the altar. I had to protect it from what Susan and the committee were doing, and it was all up to me. I had so much energy, just buzzing around like a bee, and that is when my mother was there. She was there guiding me because the work was so important. 

But then... well, eventually, my mood just completely dropped. It was like someone pulled the plug out of the wall. I just deflated entirely. I felt so incredibly sad, just sitting in my damask armchair for days on end, feeling this awful, crushing guilt that I hadn't done enough, that I had failed the church and let everyone down. It was a terrible, heavy feeling, just weeping over my tea. 

But the important thing is, doctor—and this is why I know I'm not just losing my mind like my husband thinks—once my mood dropped down like that, and I was just sitting there feeling guilty and miserable... I wasn't hearing my mother's voice anymore. I didn't see her standing in the kitchen in her housecoat. All of that just stopped completely. I was still sad, yes, and I still felt guilty, but I was not hearing or seeing those things anymore. It only happened when I was rushing around without sleep, trying to fulfill my duty to the altar. So it’s not just some constant madness, it was tied to that specific time.

We raised enough money for a new roof in 2012 because of my silent auction idea! You don't just 'forget' to ask someone who did all that, unless it's on purpose. Unless you're trying to push them out. \n\nSo no, I don't think I'm wrong. I don't think it's just me misunderstanding things. People don't want to see it because it's ugly, doctor. My husband doesn't want to see it because it means confronting his own family, and he hates conflict. He’d rather just watch his golf and pretend everything is fine. But I can't pretend. I know what they're doing with the committee, I know what they're doing at the altar, and I know they want me gone and forgotten.\n\nDoctor: Have you taken any steps to address what you believe is happening, like confronting your in-laws or speaking to someone in the church about it?\n\nPatient: Well, no, not exactly. A beautiful rump roast with carrots and potatoes, cooked low and slow all afternoon, and my gravy—well, people used to ask for the recipe, but I never gave it out. But now? Well, let me think... yes, I suppose there was the community heritage festival late last summer. Or was it early September? No, it was definitely August, I remember because the humidity was just dreadful, absolutely ruining my hair, but I didn't even care at the time because I was so entirely focused on our family's presentation. 

You see, our family has always had a major presence at this festival, it’s practically a cornerstone of the whole town's history. But my cousins and my nieces? They were just going to throw together some cheap, store-bought decorations and maybe bake a few boxed cakes. Boxed cakes! For a heritage festival! Can you even imagine the embarrassment? 

I was horrified. And in that moment, I just... I had this absolute, crystal-clear realization. I truly believed, with every fiber of my being, that I was the only one who could save our family's traditions. I mean, nobody else had the vision, doctor. Nobody else understood the stakes! I could see exactly how it all needed to be done, down to the exact draping of our grandmother's heirloom quilts and the precise way the homemade blackberry preserves needed to be stacked on the tables to catch the afternoon sun. 

I tried to explain it to them. I sat them all down at my dining room table and I said, very clearly, that if they just listened to me—if they would just step aside, follow my instructions to the letter, and let me direct everything—the whole community event would be absolutely perfect. Not just our family's booth, but the *entire* festival! Because I knew exactly how to elevate the whole thing. I had this incredible, undeniable certainty that my ideas were exactly what the town needed to make it the most spectacular jubilee in fifty years. 

But do you think they agreed with me? Of course not. My cousin Martha actually rolled her eyes and told me I was getting "too big for my britches" and acting like I was the Queen of England. Can you imagine? I was offering them absolute perfection! I knew I was the only one capable of making it a masterpiece, I had the exact blueprint for success right there in my head, but they just looked at me like I was speaking a foreign language. They just couldn't see what I was capable of, even when I was the only one trying to save them from total mediocrity.

I’d march right up and say, \"I see what you’re doing with the altar, and I see what you're doing with the committee!\" But... if I actually say it out loud to them, they’ll just do exactly what you just tried to do, doctor. They’ll tell me I’m making things up. They’ll use it as more ammunition. \n\nThey *want* me to make a scene. That’s part of the plan, don’t you see? If I march up to the parish committee during their Wednesday night bingo prep—and by the way, I was the one who organized the prize baskets for bingo for years, driving all over town getting donations from the local businesses down on Main Street, spending my own gas money—if I go down there and confront them, they’ll just look at each other, give those little knowing nods, and say, \"Oh, look at her, she’s making a fuss again.\" That is exactly what they want! They want me to look unstable so they have an excuse to erase me completely and justify everything they've been doing behind my back. \n\nSo, no. I haven't given them the satisfaction. I haven't said a single word to them about it because I know better than to walk right into their trap. I just sit back, and I watch them. I see it all happening, and I keep track of it. Every little slight, every ignored greeting, every time they change the schedule without telling me... I see it, but I haven't confronted them because that's exactly the opening they're waiting for.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had other beliefs or experiences that you were sure were real, but others told you weren’t true or didn’t make sense?\n\nPatient: Well, if you're asking if my husband thinks I'm seeing things or making things up, then yes, I suppose there is something else. Well, yes, I suppose people might say that. My husband certainly had plenty to say about my behavior, though he rarely understands the half of it! I’ve gone over it a hundred times in my head. I’d march right up and say, \"I see what you’re doing with the altar, and I see what you're doing with the committee!\" But... if I actually say it out loud to them, they’ll just do exactly what you just tried to do, doctor. They want me to look unstable so they have an excuse to erase me completely and justify everything they've been doing behind my back. \n\nSo, no. I haven't given them the satisfaction. Oh, sleep... well, that's a whole other story, doctor, it really is. It has been completely turned upside down.

I mean, I was practically handing them the keys to the most spectacular festival this town had ever seen, because I was the only one who understood what our ancestors would have wanted. But they just couldn't see my purpose, doctor, they just couldn't comprehend it!\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of time, lasting at least two weeks, when you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?\n\nPatient: Well, yes... and it's just such a terrible contrast, doctor, it really is. Because after all that energy I was just telling you about—the festival, the altar, all those grand plans and that absolute certainty—after all of that finally left me, it was like someone came along and pulled the plug right out of the wall. \n\nFor weeks now, well over two weeks, I have been waking up with this heavy, heavy sadness. It's like a physical weight pressing down on my chest before I even open my eyes in the morning. I used to be up with the sun, you know, making my coffee, getting a head start on the dusting or polishing the silver before the phone even started ringing. But lately, I just lie there in the dark. I look up at the ceiling and I can't find a single reason to push the covers back. \n\nIt's just this profound emptiness. I see the dust settling on the mantelpiece, and I just don't care. I don't care about the church committee anymore, I don't care what Helen is whispering to the rest of the family, I don't care about any of it. \n\nIt’s just a completely suffocating feeling, doctor, to go from feeling so bright and capable to feeling like a hollowed-out shell in your own home. You spend your whole life building a warm, inviting place, and then suddenly you're just sitting there completely drained of every last drop of happiness... it's just miserable, truly miserable. I wouldn't wish this kind of heavy, dark feeling on my worst enemy.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when you felt you needed much less sleep than usual, even though you still had plenty of energy and didn't feel tired?\n\nPatient: Oh, sleep... well, that's a whole other story, doctor, it really is. I just lie awake in the dark, staring up at the ceiling, and my chest just feels so tight because I am just worrying and worrying. Well, extraordinary is a strong word, doctor, but... yes, in a way, absolutely. Because, you see, I realized during all of this that I was the only one—the absolute only person in this entire parish—who could actually save our family's traditions. I mean, nobody else had the vision for it. Nobody else understood what was truly at stake!

I had the knowledge. I had the exact blueprint for perfection. And it just drove me absolutely up the wall that they couldn't see it. If they had just stopped their petty whispering and followed my instructions to the letter, everything would have been glorious.
